Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

DBinventory 0.1.7

  • Report: a diagram explains freshness (the newest date a table holds, and tables placed on a timeline) above the phase 1 freshness chart.

DBinventory 0.1.6

  • Report: a diagram of primary and foreign key candidates heads the phase 3 tab, and the sampled-run note shows what a sampled check reviewed against a full one.

DBinventory 0.1.5

  • The report’s sampled-run notes guide the reader: phase 1 is complete and usable, and a full (not sampled) check shows phase 2 onwards.

DBinventory 0.1.4

  • The report’s phase 2 tab opens with diagrams of how tables are matched, what counts as the same data, and what the labels mean.

DBinventory 0.1.3

  • Phase 2, table clustering: cluster_tables() matches columns across tables by what they hold, scores table pairs by containment, labels each related pair (copy, filtered subset, wider derivative, narrower, aggregate), groups related tables into clusters and proposes a canonical member with a rationale; every table also gets a class (event, reference, aggregate). write_cluster_decisions() and read_cluster_decisions() keep the owners’ review in a CSV that overrides the proposals on later runs. inventory_run() gains schema_priority and decisions.
  • Phases 2 and 3 are gated on a full run: on a sampled run, clustering and foreign key inference are skipped and the report says so.
  • The report is tabbed by phase: inventory and profile, table clusters, keys.

DBinventory 0.1.2

  • Report tables offer dropdown filters for columns with few distinct values (schema, type class, semantic type, flags), a rows-per-page menu and highlighted search matches, all through DT.

DBinventory 0.1.1

  • DuckDB samples large tables (100,000 rows or more) with vector-level percentage sampling instead of a reservoir sample, which scanned and rewrote the table before profiling it. Smaller tables keep the exact reservoir sample.
  • The example reports are called “sampled” and “full”; sample_rows = Inf gives the full report.

DBinventory 0.1.0

First working version.

  • Inventory: db_inventory() lists every table and column with exact row counts, sizes from system views where readable, and the newest datetime per table as a freshness signal.
  • Column profile: db_profile() records null rate, distinct count, uniqueness, min, max, mean, string lengths and top values per column, with an inferred semantic type, pk_candidate, and two fingerprint hashes. Literal values are suppressed for free text, large identifier columns and personal-data column names unless keep_values = TRUE.
  • Foreign keys: infer_foreign_keys() proposes, for each column, the key column it most looks like a reference to, with a confidence score and the evidence behind it. Candidates only, for the key register to confirm.
  • Dialects for Microsoft SQL Server (the main target), DuckDB, SQLite and PostgreSQL; db_connect() takes a connection string, DSN, SQLite or DuckDB file, or Parquet files and directories; parquet_connect() exposes a Parquet directory as a DuckDB database.
  • SQLite results store with per-table checkpointing and resume, CSV and Parquet export, and inventory_run() to do everything in one call.
  • Quarto report (render_report()) with ggplot2 plots, candidate duplicate columns, foreign key candidates and a searchable column profile; the title takes an organisation prefix.
  • Developed against the Fake NHS Trust synthetic dataset through the fakehospdata package; tests run offline on a small fixture.
